name: Antotijah
title: Descendant of Benjamin and son of Shashak
summary: Antotija is a person mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles, where he is listed as one of the sons of Shashak. Together with his brothers, he is counted among the family heads who lived in Jerusalem. His name likely bears a connection to the city of Anatoth, a Levitical town in the territory of the tribe of Benjamin, and the theophoric ending -jah links him to the divine name YHWH. Although we do not know specific actions from his life, his place in the genealogy reflects the careful preservation of Israel's tribal and family traditions, which were crucial for identity and inheritance rights in the Israelite community.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Genealogy of Benjamin
keyEvents.description: Antotijah is listed as a son of Shashak in the genealogy of the tribe of Benjamin, recorded in the Books of Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: Shashak's Sons Who Were Heads in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Antotijah was among the sons of Shashak who were counted as heads of their families. These heads resided in Jerusalem, testifying to the family's significance and position.

versions.summary: Antotijah is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles as a descendant of Benjamin. He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin and has limited information beyond his place in the family tree. His name may mean 'the Lord's answer,' and he belonged to one of Israel's twelve tribes.
versions.title: Descendant of Benjamin
versions.reason: [major] Anathoth is mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chr 8, but these genealogies extend back to the patriarchal period and up to the return from exile. It is unclear exactly when Anathoth lived, but the context in 1 Chr 8:28 suggests that these family heads lived in Jerusalem, which could fit several periods. 'divided-kingdom' is acceptable as an estimate, but it is uncertain.; [critical] According to 1 Chr 8:24-25, Anathoth was a son of Shashak. The ID 'sjasjakj' contains an extra 'j' at the end. The correct ID should be 'sjasjak'.; [major] According to 1 Chr 8:24-27, Shashak's sons are more than the four listed. The biblical text mentions among others Jifdeja, Pnuel, Elifelet, as well as several others such as Sjamsjeraj, Sjekharja, Atalja, Jaaresja, Elia and Sikri. The list of siblings should be expanded.; [minor] Although Anathoth is a less known person, the roles should contain at least one role, for example 'Family Head' or 'Descendant of Benjamin', based on the context in 1 Chr 8:28 where these are referred to as heads of their clans.; [minor] The summary is fine, but the phrasing 'His name may mean "The Lord's answer"' is uncertain etymology. The name Anathoth (אַנְתֹתִיָּה) is more likely connected to the city of Anatot and may mean 'answer from YHWH' or 'belonging to Anatot'. This should be phrased more cautiously.; [minor] The second key event ('Benjamin's descendants in Jerusalem') with verse 1 Chr 8:1-3 is very general and refers to the beginning of Benjamin's genealogy, not directly to Anathoth. This is of little relevance as a key event for this person.; [minor] Footnotes are missing. At least one footnote should be added about the name's connection to the city of Anatot (a Levitical city in Benjamin) or about the function of the genealogies in Chronicles.

versions.summary: Antotija is a person mentioned in First Chronicles as a son of Shashak and a descendant of Benjamin. He is listed in the genealogy of Benjamin among family heads who lived in Jerusalem. His name is likely connected to the city of Anatoth, a Levitical town in the territory of the tribe of Benjamin, with the ending -ja pointing to God's name (YHWH). Although little is known about him beyond his place in the family tree, his inclusion in the genealogy testifies to the importance of preserving Israel's tribal identity and family lines.
versions.title: Descendant of Benjamin and son of Shashak
versions.reason: [minor] The description states that Shashak's sons 'lived in Jerusalem,' but verse 28 says these were heads who lived in Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify that this refers to the family heads generally, not necessarily every son individually.; [minor] The interpretation 'YHWH is from Anatot' or 'Anatot's Lord' is somewhat speculative. A more neutral phrasing such as 'Anatot belonging to YHWH' or 'one from Anatot (with a theophoric element)' would be linguistically more precise.

footnotes.text: The name Antotijah (Hebrew: אַנְתֹתִיָּה) is likely derived from the city of Anatot, a Levitical city in the territory of the tribe of Benjamin (Josh 21:18). Anatot is also known as the hometown of the prophet Jeremiah (Jer 1:1). The name ending -ijah is a shortened form of the divine name YHWH, making it a theophoric compound, possibly meaning 'Yahweh's answer' or 'one from Anatot who belongs to Yahweh.'

The genealogies in 1 Chronicles served an important function after the return from the Babylonian exile. They were used to confirm Israelite tribal affiliation, property rights, and service roles, especially for Levites and priests. The fact that Shashak's sons are described as heads who lived in Jerusalem (1 Chr 8:28) shows their social status and connection to the administrative center.

Anatot is identified with the archaeological site of Ras el-Kharrube near the village of Anata, about 5 km northeast of Jerusalem. Excavations have confirmed settlement from the Bronze Age onward, consistent with the city's role in biblical texts.

The city of Anatot is mentioned several times in the Hebrew Bible. It was assigned to the Levites of the Kohathite clan (Josh 21:18) and was the home of several notable figures, including two of David's warriors: Abiezer from Anatot (2 Sam 23:27) and Jehu from Anatot (1 Chr 12:3). The city's connection to the tribe of Benjamin makes it natural for a personal name with this association to appear in Benjamin's genealogy.
